changes_made.explanation: Removed NLG tasks that were only mentioned in related work but not actually studied. Removed duplicate/redundant dataset names. Kept only the core task of hallucination detection for free-form text generation.
Corrected answer from 'No' to 'Yes' since the paper uses multiple automatic metrics to evaluate hallucination detection performance. Normalized metric names to standard capitalization.
No LLMs were used as judges - the paper uses human annotators and automatic metrics for evaluation.

guideline: Annotators determine whether perturbed text spans are hallucination (H) or not hallucination (N) based on factualness and semantic coherence with the original text given the context

The annotators were asked to determine whether the perturbed text spans are H (hallucination) or N (not hallucination) with the original text in terms of factualness and semantic coherence given the context.
Annotators decide if each highlighted span is a hallucination (H) or not (N) based on factualness and semantic coherence with the original text.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated redundant guideline descriptions into one clear statement. Normalized criteria capitalization.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on token-level reference-free hallucination detection rather than traditional NLG tasks. It evaluates hallucination detection models using both human annotations and automatic metrics. The main contribution is the HADES dataset and baseline models for fine-grained hallucination detection.
